summary: Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, having studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. His academic posts included Jena (1800), École Centrale de Cologne (~1804–1806), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies after studying at Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1790). He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1806) and a chair at the University of Berlin (~1810–1834).
Friedrich Schrader was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He completed his dissertation under Richard Pischel at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg between ~1887 and 1889.

Friedrich Weller worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, earning his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at Leipzig University under August Conrady. He held Indology chairs at Leipzig (1928, 1938–1958) and was a member of the Saxon Academy (1943–1980).

Friedrich Wilhelm is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. After studying at Munich under Paul Thieme (~1953–1956), he worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences (~1958–1964) and served as Privatdozent (1963) and Professor (1969–1998) at Munich.
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held academic positions at the University of Augsburg (~1992–1999) and the University of Munich (~1999–2014).

Philosopher Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling studied at Tübingen and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845), and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences (1827–1842).
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (~1889–1893) and Karl Foy.
Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Halle (~1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (from 1839), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Scholar of Indology and Iranian studies Friedrich Windischmann studied at Bonn—under Lassen, A. W. Schlegel, and others—and Munich. He held a professorship at Munich (1838–1839) and was General Vicar of the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1839–1861).

Friedrich Zarncke was a linguist who studied at Rostock and Leipzig, where his teachers included Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He held a post at Rostock (~1848–1850) before becoming Rektor (1852) and full professor (1858) at Leipzig University.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology after studying at Leipzig University (1787–1790). He was an honorary professor at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), director at Vienna (1824), and held a post at Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian and Indological studies. After studying at Erlangen, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena under scholars including Lassen, Brockhaus, and Fleischer, he was a professor of Oriental languages at Erlangen-Nürnberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal specialized in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, earning degrees from Amsterdam and Banaras/Madras. He held posts at SOAS (1958–1962), the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967), and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy, having studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Philosopher Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1934), the University of Munich (1936–1941), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Frédéric Baudry, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian and administrative posts at the Institut agronomique de Versailles (1849), Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).
Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Meiji University (~1928–1931) and under Xiong Shili (~1943–1949), later holding a post at Tunghai University (~1955–1969).
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1952–1956). He held academic posts at Fukuoka University (~1974–2004) and Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and also studied under Yusho Miyasaka, Zuiho Yamaguchi, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Kaiun Shiradate.
